restatements.text: Prohibits physicians from performing an abortion after 15 weeks of gestation, except when it is necessary to prevent the death of the pregnant woman or a serious risk of substantial and irreversible physical impairment of a major bodily function.

analysis.answer: Under current law, abortion is lawful up until fetal viability. The proposed measure changes this by prohibiting physicians from performing abortions after 15 weeks of gestation, allowing exceptions only to prevent the death of the pregnant woman or to avoid serious and irreversible physical impairment of a major bodily function.

Physicians and hospitals may alter their practices or frequently consult legal counsel before intervening in complex pregnancies near or past the 15-week mark to avoid potential liability. Patients seeking abortions after 15 weeks may travel to jurisdictions with different laws, if they have the resources to do so.

The measure addresses the moral and policy debate surrounding abortion by restricting the procedure earlier in pregnancy to protect fetal life. The 15-week ban mechanism directly reduces abortions post-15 weeks, though it creates a strict legal threshold that may restrict access for patients who discover severe fetal anomalies or face sudden health complications later in pregnancy.

The public health effects of gestational limits are disputed. Some researchers find that such bans increase maternal mortality and morbidity and cause reproductive health providers to leave the state. Other researchers dispute these findings, arguing that the medical emergency exceptions are sufficient to protect maternal health and that the data does not conclusively establish an exodus of medical professionals.

flags.quote: serious risk of substantial and irreversible physical impairment of a major bodily function
flags.note: The phrasing uses multiple overlapping qualifiers ('serious,' 'substantial,' 'irreversible,' 'major') without explicitly defining what medical conditions meet all these criteria, potentially leaving physicians uncertain about when the exception applies.
